/about-fore-ladies-golf.body_html:
Fore Ladies Golf – Women’s golf clothing doesn’t have to be a hazard!

I know what women want, because I AM a woman!

First and foremost, thank you for supporting my woman-owned business! The premise behind my company is simple—confidence is paramount on the golf course, and more often than not, that starts with our clothes. Anyone who plays knows that golf is just as much a mental game as physical, and the truth of the matter is, when we look good, we feel good. I am totally committed to providing women golfers with high-quality women’s golf clothes in the styles that make them feel confident.

I am a golfer, and as a big believer that our personal sense of style is reflective of our personalities, I found it difficult to find golf clothes in big box stores that suited me. I tried shopping online, but had trouble there as well. I knew then and there that if I was having trouble finding cute golf outfits, other women were, too. It was at that moment that Fore Ladies Golf was conceived.

I took my background in writing, web development, and marketing and created what you see here today. I truly love what I'm doing each and every day — helping female golfers look and feel their best on the golf course — and I enjoy putting a personal touch on all of my customer relationships... yours and mine included! If you're looking for something specific, please email me and I'll do my best to track it down. If an outfit you ordered doesn't seem to fit correctly, give me a call and I'll get you the correct size or work with you to get it altered. Not sure about the fit, length, weight, or color of something? I'll do my best to get you the information you need! My mission is to provide the personal service that you deserve, and golf clothing that will reflect you.

What’s your personal style?

Are you a pants or long shorts and a polo on the course kind of gal? Or, do you prefer to allow your personal style to shine through flirty skorts and bold patterns and colors? I am here for you both. From your traditional white, black, or grey ladies golf pants and short-sleeve shirts with collars all the way through mid-thigh skorts with ruffles and sleeveless tops in bright hues, I’ve got you covered!

Brands Fore Ladies Golf has carried

Over the years the Fore Ladies catalog has included women’s golf clothing and accessories from popular brands such as:

Newer additions to the catalog

I have also added a varied selection of both plus size and petite golf clothes!

Have a question or concern? Feel free to reach out any time!

Thank you for supporting a woman-owned business!

Jessica

Founder and owner of Fore Ladies Golf

/petite-womens-golf-clothes.body_html:
As in every type of clothing, one size does not fit all! On petite women, standard golf clothes can fit awkwardly, but these petite ladies golf clothes solve two problems at once — fashion and fit.

Why standard golf clothing fits petite frames badly

The problem with buying a smaller size is that clothing is not scaled uniformly. When a brand grades a garment down, it shortens the body far less than it narrows it. The result is familiar to anyone under about 5'4": pants that pool over the shoe, a skort that sits closer to the knee than intended, sleeves that reach past the wrist, and a shoulder seam that has slipped halfway down the upper arm.

None of this is only cosmetic. A shoulder seam in the wrong place restricts rotation at exactly the point in the swing where you need it. A sleeve that is too long catches on the follow-through. Trouser hems that drag pick up water from morning dew and get stepped on walking uphill. Petite-specific cuts fix the proportions rather than just the measurements, which is why they feel different rather than merely smaller.

What to look for in petite golf apparel

Four measurements matter more than the size on the label. Inseam is the most important for pants — golf pants are cut deliberately long to sit over a shoe, so a standard inseam on a petite frame is usually several inches too much. Skort and skirt length is measured from the waist, and a 16-inch skort designed for a 5'8" frame lands very differently on a 5'2" one; going shorter is often the correct move rather than a stylistic one.

Sleeve length and armhole placement determine whether a top lets you swing. Torso length decides whether a dress sits at your natural waist or below it. When you are shopping, check those four against a garment you already own and love, rather than trusting the size label.

Brands and styles that work

Amy Sport Petites, sometimes listed as Spitfire Petites, designs specifically for shorter frames rather than grading down from a standard block, which is the difference that matters. Within the wider collection, certain styles also work well on petite frames regardless of whether they carry a petite label.

Cropped and ankle pants are a natural fit, because a cut that reads as cropped on a taller frame often falls at full length on a petite one. Look at ankle-length styles from Daily Sports, and at cropped pants across the range. Skorts in the shorter 15- and 16-inch lengths generally sit better than longer cuts. Sleeveless tops sidestep the sleeve-length problem entirely, and are worth defaulting to in warm weather. Dresses with a defined or adjustable waist are more forgiving than straight shift cuts, which tend to drop the waistline.

For outer layers, vests are an easier buy than jackets, because there are no sleeves to get wrong. If you do buy a jacket, prioritise the shoulder fit above everything else — sleeves can be altered, shoulders effectively cannot.

Alterations worth making

A good tailor is a petite golfer's most valuable resource, and golf clothing takes alteration better than most people assume. Hemming pants is straightforward and inexpensive, and it transforms how a pair looks. Shortening sleeves on a knit or woven top is usually simple. Taking in a side seam on a polo is routine.

What does not alter well: anything with a technical laminate or taped seam, anything where the shoulder is wrong, and pleated skorts, where the pleat structure runs the full length and cannot be shortened without rebuilding the garment. If a piece needs work in those areas, it is the wrong piece.

One useful habit is to buy for the widest part of your body and alter the length. Length is the easy fix; width is not.

Proportion and how things look

Beyond fit, a few choices make petite proportions read well on the course. Keeping the waistline visible — with a tucked top, a belt, or a defined-waist dress — establishes where your body divides and makes legs look longer. Vertical elements help: a long cardigan or vest, a front placket, or a column of colour from top to bottom.

Scale matters in prints. Very large prints can overwhelm a smaller frame, while small and mid-scale patterns sit better. This is a guideline rather than a rule, and plenty of petite golfers wear bold prints extremely well — but if a print has ever felt like it was wearing you, scale is usually why.

Shoes contribute too. A shoe that matches your pant or skort colour extends the line of the leg, while a contrasting shoe cuts it. Browse our golf shoes collection with that in mind.

Shopping online when you are petite

Measure yourself once, properly, and write the numbers down: bust, natural waist, hip, inseam and torso length. Then compare against the brand-specific measurements on our size charts rather than assuming a size carries across brands. It does not.

When two sizes are plausible, the smaller one is usually right for a petite frame if the measurements allow, because excess fabric reads as ill-fitting faster on a shorter body. Our returns policy covers new, unworn items within 30 days, so ordering the one you think is right and returning it if it is not is a reasonable strategy on non-final-sale items.

One last thought: fit problems on a petite frame are a manufacturing issue, not a personal one. Clothing is graded from a standard block that simply does not describe every body, and a garment that hangs badly is telling you about the pattern rather than about you. Buy for the measurements you have, alter what needs altering, and ignore the number on the label.

Can't find what you need?

Petite golf apparel is still under-served by the industry, and we know the selection is smaller than it should be. If you are looking for something specific — a particular inseam, a shorter skort, a brand you have had luck with before — tell us through our contact page and we will try to track it down. We would rather find it for you than have you settle.

You can also browse our plus size collection, bottoms, tops and golf dresses for pieces that work across a range of proportions.

/playforpink.body_html:
Paying it fore-ward

When you make a purchase through Fore Ladies Golf and use the code PINK at checkout, you not only save 10% on your order as our thank you for supporting the cause, we in turn donate 10% of your purchase directly to Play for P.I.N.K.

Much of what we do on a day-to-day basis centers around those in our immediate circle — our family, our friends, and our neighbors. When they need our help, we make it our mission to give and do whatever it takes to improve their situation, whether that means we pick up an extra errand for them, help them with a household project, or slip a couple extra bucks into their hand. We are givers, nurturers, and caretakers for those we love, and it often brings us immeasurable joy.

Each and every day, we are bombarded with social media stories of people "paying it forward", "giving back", and "making a difference". How many times have you read of someone whose drink was paid for at the local coffee shop, or a good samaritan who stopped to help entertain a code-red-tantruming toddler in the checkout line? These stories are more than heart warming for us at Fore Ladies Golf. They're inspirational. They make us think about how our interactions with others can potentially change the tone of someone's day, and cause a ripple effect of good will that could never be quantified. These stories inspire us to do MORE.

In the spirit of doing more, we struck out to find a way to affect lives on a broader scale, and as luck would have it, we didn't need to search for very long. When LPGA Women Who Play NJ contacted us about a sponsorship opportunity, I recognized a real potential to pay it forward, give back, AND make a difference... and on a broader scale. After speaking with them one on one, a plan began to come together.

The partnership

Most of us know at least one person who has or has had breast cancer, I realize what a personal cause it is for so many, and for that reason, I am delighted to share that Fore Ladies Golf is partnering with Play for P.I.N.K. to help fund breast cancer research. For more than 20 years, Play for P.I.N.K. has been helping to organize golf, tennis, and other active events throughout the U.S. with the sole purpose of raising money to fund research. In that time, they have had over 30,000 participants and have donated nearly $53,000,000 to the Breast Cancer Research Foundation!

Join us!

When you make a purchase through Fore Ladies Golf and use the code PINK at checkout, you not only save 10% on your order as our thank you for supporting the cause, we in turn donate 10% of your purchase directly to Play for P.I.N.K.

We thank you for your continued support, and hope you are enjoying your season!

Sincerely,

Jessica — Founder of Fore Ladies Golf

/shipping-returns.body_html:
Apparel Returns Policy

You may return new, unworn items within 30 days of delivery for a refund (minus return shipping costs). Gift certificates are not able to be refunded.

Returns details:

  • Items returned with deodorant on them will have a $10 laundering charge deducted from the refund.
  • Returns initiated after 30 days will result in a store credit.
  • If you are requesting an exchange, please include that information with your return package.
  • To initiate a return or exchange, please use our contact formand request a return authorization.

Refund details:

You should expect to receive your refund within 2 weeks of giving your package to the return shipper. This time period includes the transit time for us to receive your return from the shipper, the time it takes us to process your return, and the time it takes your bank to process our refund request.

Refunds to your original form of payment (minus shipping costs*) are applied for new, unworn items received within 30 days of delivery.

As a small business, we would appreciate the opportunity to serve you again! Request a store credit instead of a refund and we will add $5 to your refund amount!

To initiate a return or exchange, please mail unworn items with intact tags and a copy of your order confirmation to:

Fore Ladies Golf
1800 Westbrook Ct
Plainfield, IL 60586

Your return will be processed within 14 days of receipt.

Tee Box Policy

We do not accept returns on Tee Box subscription boxes or gift boxes — all sales are final. Boxes returned to us will not be eligible for a refund. Size exchanges for Tee Box apparel can be requested by filling out this form: Tee Box Size Exchanges

Shipping

Non-Tee Box items are typically shipped within 1-2 business days of receiving your order. Most orders are shipped using USPS, with heavier orders being shipped via UPS.

Tee Boxes (subscription boxes) are shipped during the first week of every month. Boxes purchased after the 15th of the month will ship as part of the following month's subscription.

Your tracking number will be sent via system message as soon as it's available.

International Shipping

We will ship internationally, however, any customs fees incurred are the responsibility of the recipient. Please familiarize yourself with the customs guidelines in your country before placing an order.

Thank you for supporting our small, woman-owned and operated business!

/womens-golf-clothes-size-charts.body_html:
How to measure yourself properly — once

Almost every sizing problem in online clothes shopping traces back to a guess. Spend ten minutes with a soft tape measure and a note on your phone, and you will buy more accurately for years. Measure over the underwear you would normally wear, keep the tape snug but not tight, and keep it level all the way round.

Bust: around the fullest part, with the tape level across your back. Natural waist: the narrowest point of your torso, usually just above the navel — bend sideways and the crease that forms is your natural waist. Hip: around the fullest part of your hips and seat, usually about 20cm below the waist. Inseam: from the crotch seam to where you want the hem to fall, measured on a pair of pants you already like rather than on your leg. Torso length: from the top of your shoulder, over the bust, down to your natural waist — this is the measurement that decides whether a dress sits where it should.

Write all five down. When a size chart gives you two plausible options, these numbers settle it.

Why golf brands size so differently

There is no shared standard. A size 8 from a Scandinavian brand, an American brand and an Italian brand can differ by several centimetres in the same measurement, and the differences are not consistent across the body — a brand that runs generous in the hip may run narrow in the shoulder.

Three factors drive most of the variation. First, the base block each brand designs from, which reflects the body shape it has historically fitted. Second, the intended fit — performance brands cut closer, traditional brands cut looser, and both may label the result the same size. Third, fabric stretch: a garment with four-way stretch can be cut smaller than a woven one and still fit, so the flat measurement alone does not tell the whole story.

The practical conclusion is simple. Trust the brand's own chart and your measurements, not the size you wore last time in something else. It is entirely normal to be three different sizes across three brands in your wardrobe, and it says nothing about you.

Choosing skort and skirt length

Golf skorts and skirts are listed by the length of the skirt portion, measured from the waistband down. Common lengths run from about 15 inches to about 20 inches, and the right number depends on your height and on where you want the hem to sit relative to your knee.

The reliable method is to measure a skort you already own and wear happily, then shop to that number. If you do not own one, measure from your natural waist to the point on your leg where you would like the hem, and use that. Height matters more than dress size here: the same 18-inch skort sits well above the knee on a 5'2" frame and close to it on a 5'9" one.

Many clubs and courses have dress codes that specify a minimum length, so if you play somewhere with published rules, check them before ordering. Our petite collection and plus size collection both address the cases where standard lengths do not translate well.

Pants, shorts and the inseam question

Golf pants are cut deliberately long, because they are meant to break over the top of a golf shoe rather than sit above it. This surprises people who buy their usual size and find several extra inches at the hem. It is intentional, not an error — but it does mean that inseam matters at least as much as waist size.

Check the inseam before you check the size. Many brands offer the same pant in multiple inseams, listed in the product name as a number such as 29 or 32. Shorts and cropped pants are listed the same way. If your inseam falls between two options, remember that hemming is a straightforward and inexpensive alteration while lengthening is not.

Tops, shoulders and the swing test

For tops, the shoulder is the measurement that decides whether a garment works for golf. A shoulder seam should sit at the outer edge of your shoulder bone. If it has slipped down your arm, the top is too large through the upper body regardless of how it fits at the waist, and it will bind when you rotate.

When a top arrives, do the swing test before you remove the tags. Stand as you would at address, make a slow, full backswing and follow-through, then reach across your body. If the fabric pulls across the shoulder blades, rides up at the front, or the cuff drags over the back of your hand, it is the wrong size or the wrong cut. A top that passes that test will be comfortable for eighteen holes.

Sleeveless styles remove the sleeve variable entirely and are the most forgiving choice if you are uncertain, which is one reason they dominate summer golf wardrobes.

Dresses and one-piece fit

Golf and tennis dresses are the hardest garment to size online, because they have to fit the bust, the waist and the hip simultaneously, and the torso length has to be right as well. If a brand's chart gives a dress length or a torso measurement, use it — it tells you more than the size does.

Styles with a defined or adjustable waist, a wrap front, or an elasticated seam are considerably more forgiving than a straight shift. If you are between sizes in a dress, the larger size is usually the safer choice, since a dress that is slightly loose can be belted while one that is tight across the hip cannot be fixed.

Shoes: width matters as much as length

Golf shoe sizing varies between European and American systems, and conversions are not always consistent between brands. Measure your foot at the end of the day when it is at its largest, and measure both feet — most people have one slightly larger, and the shoe should fit that one.

Width is the measurement people most often ignore and most often need. If golf shoes have consistently felt tight across the ball of your foot, the answer is a wider fit rather than a longer shoe. Going up a size to solve a width problem gives you a shoe that slides at the heel, which costs you stability in the swing. There is more on this in our golf shoes collection.

What to do when you are between sizes

There is no universal rule, but there are useful defaults. For bottoms, size to your largest relevant measurement — usually hip — and alter the waist if needed. For tops, size to the shoulder. For dresses, size up. For anything with significant stretch, size down. For anything marked final sale, ask us first rather than guessing.

Our returns policy covers new, unworn items within 30 days of delivery, which means that on regular-price items, ordering the size you believe is right and returning it if it is not is a perfectly reasonable approach.

Still not sure? Ask us

Charts cannot answer everything. If you want a flat garment measurement, the fabric composition, or an honest opinion on how a particular style runs, get in touch through our contact page. We will measure the actual piece rather than quote the chart back at you. Finding the right size the first time is better for you and better for us.

"It’s not about the size you wear but the way you wear your size."
